payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1, every real number x, and every integer m, one has E_n(x + m) = E_n(x).

result_payload.addressed_previous_feedback: No previous feedback was provided; this attempt directly proves the stated periodicity claim from the definition of E_n.
result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1, a real number x, and an integer m. By the definition of E_n(t),
E_n(t)=floor(nt)-\sum_{k=1}^n floor(kt)/k.
We evaluate this at t=x+m.

For the first term, nx+nm differs from nx by the integer nm, so floor(n(x+m))=floor(nx+nm)=floor(nx)+nm.
For each k in {1,\dots,n}, the number km is an integer, hence floor(k(x+m))=floor(kx+km)=floor(kx)+km.
Therefore
E_n(x+m)=floor(nx)+nm-\sum_{k=1}^n (floor(kx)+km)/k.
Since (floor(kx)+km)/k = floor(kx)/k + m, this becomes
E_n(x+m)=floor(nx)+nm-\sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k-\sum_{k=1}^n m.
But \sum_{k=1}^n m = nm, so the nm terms cancel:
E_n(x+m)=floor(nx)-\sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k = E_n(x).
Thus E_n(x+m)=E_n(x) for all real x and all integers m.
result_payload.proof_summary: Use the integer-shift identity for the floor function termwise: floor(k(x+m)) = floor(kx)+km. The added km/k = m contributions cancel against the shift in floor(nx), proving periodicity with period 1.
